papers.headline: Coronal Mass Ejections from the Young Sun: Deceleration-Powered Solar Energetic Particles as a Self-Extinguishing Forcing of the Early Earth
papers.summary: At ∼3.9 Ga (stellar age ∼0.6 Gyr), the young Sun was far more magnetically active than today. It launched ∼10² large, fast coronal mass ejections (CMEs) per year into a denser, more magnetized wind.
papers.title: Coronal Mass Ejections from the Young Sun: Deceleration-Powered Solar Energetic Particles as a Self-Extinguishing Forcing of the Early Earth

papers.headline: Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys (COMPASS) – IV. Methyl cyanide isotopologues toward BHR71-IRS1
papers.summary: Methyl cyanide is one of the most abundant nitrogen-bearing complex organic molecules observed in the gas phase around low- and high-mass protostars.
papers.title: Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys (COMPASS) – IV. Methyl cyanide isotopologues toward BHR71-IRS1

papers.headline: Mitigating prior-volume effects in galaxy clustering by adopting Mpc over Mpc/h units
papers.summary: We investigate prior-volume effects in Bayesian analyses of galaxy clustering based on state-of-the-art models, such as the EFT and the VDG_∞ model.
papers.title: Mitigating prior-volume effects in galaxy clustering by adopting Mpc over Mpc/h units
